teamDashboard.title: Naples, Italy Hazards Assessment — Group Workflow
teamDashboard.subtitle: Google Sheets-ready team tracker for a five-member, 10-minute city-council presentation

projectSummary.audience: Naples City Council; assume no prior scientific knowledge
projectSummary.finalProduct: One shared slide deck for a 10-minute presentation
projectSummary.bigQuestion: How do Earth systems influence the hazards present to people living in different locations?
projectSummary.decisionQuestion: Which hazards are of greatest concern in Naples, and what actions should the city take to reduce risk?

members.primaryHandoff: Final ranking, action plan, and deck merge

teamWorkingRules: Each member works only in the assigned section until peer review.
Reuse and condense the existing Naples draft instead of rebuilding every slide.
Every content slide needs a readable visual, a one-sentence takeaway, and an author-year citation at the bottom.
Use plain language appropriate for city council members; explain scientific terms briefly.
Member 5 merges the deck after each section is marked Ready for Review or Complete.

assignments.requiredContent: Explain Africa/Nubia–Eurasia convergence, Adriatic/Apulian microplate influence, boundary style, Naples topography, and how the setting produces earthquake and volcanic hazards.
assignments.visualsRequired: Plate map; Naples regional map showing Campi Flegrei, Vesuvius, Gulf of Naples, and Apennines.
assignments.deliverable: Three polished slides with concise speaker notes and citations.
assignments.dependenciesHandoff: Send Member 2 the tectonic explanation and base-map labels; send Member 5 the one-sentence Part I takeaway.

assignments.section: Earthquakes, faults, ground response, and exposure
assignments.requiredContent: Combine earthquake type/location/magnitude/frequency, faults, surface materials, shaking amplification, liquefaction, landslides, coastal water hazards, population exposure, and economic consequences.
assignments.visualsRequired: IRIS/EarthScope seismicity map; fault map; geology/ground-response map; exposure symbols.
assignments.deliverable: Three polished slides with one map-led message per slide and citations.
assignments.dependenciesHandoff: Use Member 1 tectonic setting. Provide Member 5 with earthquake score inputs and loss assumptions.

assignments.requiredContent: Cover Campi Flegrei, Vesuvius, and Ischia; volcano type/location; photos; eruption history; 100-year probability outlook; hazards; red/yellow zones; exposed population and disaster cost.
assignments.visualsRequired: Volcano location map; Vesuvius and Campi Flegrei images; eruption timeline; evacuation-zone map.
assignments.deliverable: Three polished slides comparing the three volcanic systems.
assignments.dependenciesHandoff: Provide Member 5 with volcanic priority scores, population figures, and mitigation needs.

assignments.section: Climate change, sea-level rise, flooding, heat, and drought
assignments.requiredContent: Present 2050 and 2100 temperature/precipitation projections with confidence ranges; sea-level-rise range; compound coastal flooding; drought/heat impacts; implications for the port, drainage, health, utilities, and tourism.
assignments.visualsRequired: Climate projection graph/map; coastal inundation/flood map; impact pathway diagram.
assignments.deliverable: Three polished slides connecting projections directly to Naples neighborhoods and infrastructure.
assignments.dependenciesHandoff: Provide Member 5 with climate hazard score inputs, affected areas, and realistic mitigation actions.

assignments.section: Hazard ranking, mitigation, conclusion, and integration
assignments.requiredContent: Build a four-factor scoring algorithm; rank Campi Flegrei, major earthquake, Vesuvius, and climate flood/heat/drought; summarize human/economic costs; present a 10-year multi-hazard program, budget, effectiveness, cost-benefit, and call to action.
assignments.visualsRequired: Priority matrix; impact table; 10-year timeline; cost-benefit graphic.
assignments.deliverable: Four content slides; merge all sections; title slide; references; final quality and timing review.
assignments.dependenciesHandoff: Wait for all members to mark sections Ready for Review. Resolve duplicated content and standardize citations/design.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: City, team names, course, and one strong Naples image.
Africa/Nubia–Eurasia convergence, Adriatic/Apulian microplate, and mixed convergent/extension setting.
slides.suggestedVisual: Central Mediterranean plate map with motion arrows.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Naples lies between Campi Flegrei, Vesuvius, the Gulf of Naples, and the Apennines; dense development overlaps hazardous terrain.
slides.suggestedVisual: Regional map with labeled volcanic and geographic features.

slides.slideTitle: How the tectonic setting creates Naples hazards
slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Connect plate motion to regional earthquakes, magma generation, hydrothermal activity, and shallow volcanic earthquakes.
slides.suggestedVisual: Cause-and-effect diagram plus small hazard icons.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Cite tectonic, earthquake, and volcanic sources.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Regional Southern Apennine earthquakes versus shallow Campi Flegrei/Ischia/Vesuvius events; magnitude and frequency ranges.

slides.slideTitle: Faults, surface materials, and shaking response
slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Major regional faults; local volcanic structures; tuff, pyroclastics, alluvium/fill, and carbonate bedrock response.
Shaking amplification, liquefaction, landslides/rockfall, harbor seiche/tsunami, exposed communities, infrastructure, and economic loss.
slides.suggestedVisual: Hazard/exposure map with port, hospitals, and dense municipalities.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Campi Flegrei caldera, Vesuvius stratovolcano, and Ischia volcanic island; explain why each creates different hazards.
slides.suggestedVisual: Location map and two representative images.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Key eruptions from the Campanian Ignimbrite through 1944; explain uncertain but non-zero future eruption probability.
slides.citationSourceCheck: State that exact timing cannot be predicted.

slides.slideTitle: Volcanic hazards, vulnerable zones, and cost
slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Pyroclastic flows, ash/lapilli, bradyseism, gases, hydrothermal explosions, lahars; red-zone populations and economic disruption.
slides.suggestedVisual: Civil Protection zone map plus population callouts.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Distinguish official values from planning estimates.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Temperature rise, precipitation changes, confidence ranges, longer dry spells, and intense rainfall.
slides.suggestedVisual: Regional climate graph or map with 2050/2100 comparison.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Use model source and confidence range.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: AR6 sea-level range, local vertical land movement, compound flooding, drainage limits, and drought.

slides.slideTitle: What climate change means for Naples
slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Connect heat, flood, drought, wildfire, water stress, port exposure, tourism, health, and utilities to city decisions.
slides.suggestedVisual: Impact pathway from hazard to people and infrastructure.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Explain 1–5 scoring for exposure, human cost, economic disruption, and urgency/probability.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Identify as a classroom planning tool.

slides.slideTitle: Top four hazards and expected consequences
slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Rank Campi Flegrei, major earthquake, Vesuvius, and climate flood/heat/drought; include people affected, casualties/displacement, and economic interruption.
slides.suggestedVisual: Compact comparison table or bubble chart.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Label scenario estimates and official values.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Years 1–2 map/inspect; 2–5 protect lifelines; 3–10 drills, shelters, alerts, evacuation routes, and adaptation.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Cite Civil Protection and INGV context.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: Budget, avoided losses, lives/displacement reduced, first priorities, and a direct city-council decision request.
slides.citationSourceCheck: Mark budget as a planning range.

slides.requiredContentTakeaway: APA bibliography for every source used; include image credits and URLs.
slides.suggestedVisual: Clean one- or two-slide reference layout if needed.

timelineAndHandoffs.title: Recommended 10-Day Workflow — Replace Day Numbers with Actual Dates

phases.action: Confirm roles, slide numbers, citation style, theme, and shared-folder structure.
Review assigned draft slides and verify maps, figures, facts, and image credits.
Condense each assigned section to three slides; remove repeated explanations and long paragraphs.
Prepare the scoring framework, collect human/economic inputs, and draft mitigation structure.
Build assigned slides using the common template, citations, and one-sentence takeaways.
Check scientific accuracy, readability, citations, visuals, and overlap.
Submit corrected slides, source list, and image credits to Member 5.
Merge slides, standardize titles/fonts/colors, remove duplicates, and build references.
Run through the deck for 10 minutes; simplify technical terms and cut unnecessary text.
Run the rubric checklist, verify citations and links, test the file, and submit.

mergeChecklist.title: Naples Final Deck Merge and Rubric Checklist

items.checklistItem: All required hazards are covered: tectonics, earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides/secondary hazards, flooding, and climate change.
Four hazards are prioritized and justified against other hazards.
Population affected and killed/injured/homeless or displaced ranges are shown for each top hazard.
Port, tourism, transport, utilities, hospitals, schools, housing, and business disruption are addressed.
The strategy includes description, implementation needs, timeline, effectiveness, realistic cost, and cost-benefit.
Every major claim is supported by a map, figure, timeline, table, or diagram rather than text alone.
Terms such as bradyseism, caldera, pyroclastic flow, liquefaction, and microzonation are explained in plain language.
Every slide has author-year citation(s) in 8–10 pt text at the bottom.
Every in-slide citation and image credit appears in the APA references, with no unused references.
Fonts, title placement, colors, map labels, legends, units, and terminology are consistent.
Generalized classroom maps are labeled as generalized; scenario estimates are not presented as official forecasts.
The complete deck can be explained in 10 minutes, averaging about 30–35 seconds per content slide.
Final PPTX opens correctly; backup PDF is created; file name includes city, course, and team.
